prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Three views of the unwell child', subtitle 'Paediatric assessment triangle'. A large open equilateral triangle composed of three coloured wooden beams around a simple wooden person game token labelled 'Rapid impression'. At upper left an icon of two speech bubbles labelled 'Appearance', below 'Interaction • tone • cry'. At upper right a small unnumbered effort gauge plus sound ripples labelled 'Work of breathing', below 'Effort • sounds'. At bottom centre three abstract colour tiles, one pale, one marbled, one dusky, labelled 'Circulation to skin', below 'Colour • mottling'. Tiles are paint swatches, not diagnostic skin examples; no organs. From the triangle a clear forward arrow leads to short phrase 'Assess • act • reassess'. Do not reproduce any existing clinical poster layout; use this original object composition.

clinicalSources.title: RACGP: Assessment of the unwell child

teaching.question: What three observations form the paediatric assessment triangle?
teaching.answer: Appearance, work of breathing and circulation to skin. Together they give a rapid initial impression that informs prompt assessment, action and reassessment.

title: Three views of the unwell child
caption: The paediatric assessment triangle combines appearance, work of breathing and circulation to skin for a rapid initial impression. It leads into assessment and action, rather than replacing them.
alt: Three coloured sides of a triangle surround a wooden child token; outside icons represent interaction, breathing effort and skin colour.

review.notes: Triangle correctly locates appearance, work of breathing and circulation to skin around a non-anatomical wooden token. Supporting labels reflect interaction/tone/cry, effort/sounds, colour/mottling. Exit arrow calls for assessment, action and reassessment. Swatches are abstract paint, not purported diagnostic skin photographs; no pulse-only circulation substitution.
